L34: # Spacetime Bartnik Mass Positivity and Temporal Monotonicity for Black Holes
L35: Lars Andersson Affiliation: Kungliga Tekniska högskolan
L36:                                                 100 44 Stockholm, Sweden    Marcus Khuri Affiliation: Department of Mathematics, Stony Brook University
L37:                 Stony Brook, NY 11794, USA

L45: ###### Abstract
L46: We define a quasilocal mass of Bartnik type, and establish its positivity and temporal monotonicity properties for two classes of domains associated with black holes. More precisely, we first show that the quasilocal mass is strictly positive for spacelike hypersurfaces that are: compact with apparent horizon boundary or noncompact with asymptotically flat ends and containing an apparent horizon in any admissible extension.
L47: Secondly, we show that the quasilocal mass is monotonically nondecreasing in time within evolutionary scenarios related to the two aforementioned settings.
L48: ## 1 Introduction
L49: ### 1.1 Motivation
L50: 
L51: Gravitational energy is non-local and hence it is an interesting problem to find useful quasilocal notions of mass or energy-momentum [【22†27】]. Given a spacelike hypersurface $\Omega$ in spacetime, its quasilocal mass should measure the total mass or energy-momentum contained in $\Omega$. There are many competing definitions of quasilocal masses with interesting properties [【23†31】].
L52: Here we consider a quasilocal mass $m(\Omega)$ of Bartnik type [【24†11】, 【25†12】, 【26†13】, 【27†25】]. We recall that Bartnik’s idea is to define ‘admissible’ extensions of $\Omega$ which are asymptotically flat, and satisfy an energy condition such that the ADM masses of the extensions are well defined and nonnegative.
L53: A key issue is to find a suitable ‘no-horizons’ condition, that should render the infimum of the ADM masses at a designated end of all admissible extensions nonnegative, and positive unless the original domain $\Omega$ arises from Minkowski space. This problem can be studied in the Riemannian setting, where the no-horizons condition is expressed in terms of the absence of minimal surfaces, or in the general case of initial data sets where one might expect apparent horizons to play a role.

L15: 【6†View PDF】 【7†HTML (experimental)】
L16: > Abstract:We resolve Kroó's 2004 conjecture on homogeneous polynomial approximation in every dimension, without smoothness or curvature assumptions. For every origin-symmetric convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ with nonempty interior, every continuous real function on $\partial K$ is uniformly approximated by sums of homogeneous polynomials of degrees $n$ and $n+1$ as $n\to\infty$.
L17: Moreover, approximation of the constant function by homogeneous polynomials of degree $2n$ is uniform over all such bodies in each fixed dimension. Via homogenization, we also resolve Kroó's 2019 weighted approximation conjecture for every convex admissible weight on Euclidean space. The key construction produces homogeneous polynomials with a common Gaussian boundary profile and localization errors controlled by arbitrary polynomial weights.
L18: Its analytic core is a weighted Gaussian approximation theorem: for \(d\ge2\), sufficiently broad Gaussians on $\mathbb R^{d-1}$ can be approximated by $e^{-f}F$, where $f$ is nonnegative, convex and Lipschitz with $f(0)=0$, and $F$ is a Schwartz function with Fourier support in an arbitrarily small ball about the origin. Small Fourier support allows Taylor truncation to a lower degree, while the remainder enforces decay through homogenization.
L19: We then use positive spherical quadrature and degree raising to yield the full approximation theorem.

L17: 【8†No PDF available, click to view other formats】
L18: > Abstract:We give a proof of the cosmological splitting conjecture of Robert Bartnik from 1988, which expresses the rigidity of the cosmological Hawking--Penrose singularity theorem. It states that a timelike geodesically complete, globally hyperbolic spacetime which has compact Cauchy surfaces and satisfies the strong energy condition must split isometrically as a Lorentzian product.
L19: Our methods combine the construction of global viscosity solutions to the Lorentzian eikonal equation by Zhu--Wu--Cui with our recently developed elliptic approach to the proof of Lorentzian splitting theorems in joint work with Braun, Gigli and Sämann, where we make use of the $p$-d'Alembertian operator for $p < 1$.
L20: Comments:  | The starting point of our withdrawn resolution to Bartnik's conjecture (our Proposition 2.2 and the reference on which it is based) is shown to be false by a counterexample of Ehrlich and Galloway (1990). We are grateful to Greg Galloway for drawing this error to our attention. See our forthcoming joint work for further examples and discussion
